subject: Re: Unexpected duplicate usage charges on Feb 11 billing
messages:
From: Adrian Cole <adrian.cole@acmecorp.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
Cc: accounts-payable@acmecorp.com
Date: 2026-02-11T09:13:00-08:00
Subject: Unexpected duplicate usage charges on Feb 11 billing

Hi Sean,

We just noticed a sizable unexpected charge on our Feb 11 statement that looks like the same heavy-usage window was billed twice. I attached a short CSV export from our side showing the two line items. Can you confirm: did Redwood double-count tokens during the outage window yesterday? Our AP team is holding the payment until we get clarification.

Thanks,
Adrian
Adrian Cole
Senior Engineering Manager, Acme Corp
adrian.cole@acmecorp.com

Attachment: usage_report-20260211.csv

From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
To: Adrian Cole <adrian.cole@acmecorp.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-02-11T10:02:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Unexpected duplicate usage charges on Feb 11 billing

Adrian —

First, I want to apologize for the confusion and the disruption to your AP workflow. We’re actively investigating on our side. Short summary up front: we experienced a token accounting edge case during a partial-serving fallback yesterday that resulted in duplicate token attribution for a subset of requests between 02:13–02:39 UTC. We’re treating this as a high-priority billing incident.

What I’m doing now:
- Looping in Marcus from Billing to validate the numbers and propose a corrected invoice.
- Preparing a formal postmortem and a proposed credit/refund for the duplicate window.
- I’ll follow up with an ETA for the corrected invoice within 48 hours.

I’ve attached the raw usage export you sent to our internal ticket so Marcus can reconcile. We’ll make this right.

Thanks for flagging it.
Sean
Sean Gallagher
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
sean.gallagher@redwood.com

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Adrian Cole <adrian.cole@acmecorp.com>
Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-02-12T14:28:00-08:00
Subject: Corrected invoice and proposed credit for Feb 11 duplicate counts

Adrian —

Thanks for the quick heads up and for the CSV. I finished a reconciliation pass against our internal accounting logs. Summary:

- Impact window: 2026-02-11T02:13:00Z — 2026-02-11T02:39:00Z
- Duplicate token count: 1,237,980 tokens (across 12 API keys)
- Gross overcharge (pre-tax): $3,716.94

Actions we are proposing:
1) Immediate credit of $3,716.94 applied to your Feb invoice.
2) Corrected invoice attached: corrected-invoice-ACME-47891.pdf. This replaces the original Feb statement and shows the applied credit and new balance.
3) We will issue a refundable payment (ACH) for the credited amount within 7 business days if you prefer a cash refund instead of credit. Please confirm preference and AP contact.

We’ve also attached our draft incident postmortem for transparency; that doc includes root cause and mitigation steps (short version: a retry de-duplication bug in the accounting layer during a multi-backend failover). We’re scheduling a customer office hour next week if you’d like a walkthrough.

Apologies again — we’ll make sure your accounts are reconciled and provide better guardrails so this doesn’t recur.

Regards,
Marcus Lin
Billing Lead, Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwood.com

Attachments: corrected-invoice-ACME-47891.pdf, incident-postmortem-20260214.md

From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
To: Adrian Cole <adrian.cole@acmecorp.com>
Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-02-13T08:45:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Corrected invoice and proposed credit for Feb 11 duplicate counts

Adrian —

Thanks for working with us on this. Quick note from CS: we’ll open a follow-up ticket to validate there were no duplicate responses served to your app (we verified duplicates were only in accounting, not payload delivery, but we’ll confirm). Also: if your AP team needs an invoice redline or a PO reference on the corrected invoice, tell me the preferred PO number and I’ll get it annotated.

If you want a walkthrough of the postmortem we can do 30 minutes early next week — Sean and Marcus can join.

Best,
Monica Patel
Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference
monica.patel@redwood.com

From: Adrian Cole <adrian.cole@acmecorp.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
Cc: accounts-payable@acmecorp.com
Date: 2026-02-15T11:02:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Corrected invoice and proposed credit for Feb 11 duplicate counts

Hi team —

Thanks for the fast turnaround and the detailed reconciliation. We confirm the corrected invoice looks right. AP prefers a cash refund for this specific line item and will need an ACH payment. Please issue the refund to the account on file for Acme (let me know if you need updated banking info).

Also: accounts-payable@acmecorp.com asked for the postmortem and a clear statement they can include with their recordkeeping — can Marcus share a one-paragraph summary and the incident postmortem link to that address?

Appreciate the clarity and the offer to walk through — we don’t need the office hour right now, but please keep us on the invite list in case internal stakeholders want it.

Thanks,
Adrian

From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
To: Adrian Cole <adrian.cole@acmecorp.com>, accounts-payable@acmecorp.com
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Mark us Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-02-16T16:45:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Corrected invoice and proposed credit for Feb 11 duplicate counts — confirmation of refund schedule

Adrian / AP team —

Confirming next steps:
- Marcus will initiate an ACH refund of $3,716.94 to the Acme account on file. Expected posting: within 5–7 business days.
- Marcus will also post the one-paragraph summary to accounts-payable@acmecorp.com with a link to the full postmortem (see below).
- Internally, Evelyn will track a follow-up to ensure de-duplication logic has a regression test and alerting (assigned).

One-paragraph summary for AP: "On 2026-02-11 between 02:13–02:39 UTC Redwood experienced a bookkeeping race condition during a multi-backend failover which caused a subset of requests to be counted twice in usage logs. Redwood validated the overcount, issued a corrected invoice, and is issuing a refund of $3,716.94. We have implemented a fix and additional regression tests to prevent recurrence; full postmortem is available at the link below."

Link to postmortem: https://redwood-internal.company/postmortems/2026-02-14-duplicate-token-count

If AP needs the refund routed to a different bank account, please send updated ACH details securely and CC me. Thanks again for your patience — we’ll follow up once the ACH posts.

Best,
Sean

Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
